1001:
Expand each summand as (x + k - 1)(x + k + 1) = x^2 + 2kx + k^2 - 1 for k = 1 to n
Sum over k using sum k = n(n + 1) / 2 and sum k^2 = n(n + 1)(2n + 1) / 6 to get total
Set total equal to 4n and divide by n to get x^2 + (n + 1)x + (n + 1)(2n + 1) / 6 - 5 = 0
Roots \alpha and \alpha + 2 give sum 2\alpha + 2 = 0 - (n + 1) so \alpha = 0 - (n + 3) / 2
Product \alpha(\alpha + 2) = (n + 3)(n - 1) / 4 equals (n + 1)(2n + 1) / 6 - 5 which simplifies to n^2 = 49
Hence n = 7 with \alpha = 0 - 5 so n + \alpha = 2 → (C)
1002:
Rationalize denominators via 2x / (1 + 3i) = x(1 - 3i) / 5 and y / (1 - 2i) = y(1 + 2i) / 5
Collect real and imaginary parts to get bracket (x - y) + i(0 - 3x - 2y) inside the factor 50
Multiply by 50 to get 10[(x - y) + i(0 - 3x - 2y)] = 31 + 17i after simplifying the factor 10
Equate parts to get x - y = 31 / 10 and 0 - 3x - 2y = 17 / 10 as two linear equations
Solve the pair to get x = 9 / 10 and y = 0 - 11 / 5 and then x - 3y = 15 / 2
Multiply by 10 to get 10(x - 3y) = 75 → (D)
1003:
Write coefficient determinant D = 1(\beta - 4\alpha) - 2(2\beta - 8\alpha) + 1(8 - 8) = 3(4\alpha - \beta)
Compute the z determinant D_z from constants 5, 5, 18 to get D_z = 1(18 - 20) - 2(36 - 40) = 6
Since D_z = 6 is never zero, the system is inconsistent exactly when D = 0 by Cramers rule
Vanishing D gives 3(4\alpha - \beta) = 0 so \beta = 4\alpha with \alpha and \beta linked
Check consistency: if \beta differs from 4\alpha then D differs from zero and a unique solution exists
If \beta equals 4\alpha then D = 0 with D_z nonzero so no solution exists for that pair
Hence no solution forces \beta / \alpha = 4 → (B)
1004:
Compute A^2 = [[3, 2 + 2\alpha],[1 + \alpha, 2 + \alpha^2]] and impose A^2 - 4A + I = O
Off diagonal gives 2 + 2\alpha - 8 = 0 so \alpha = 3 which also zeroes the other entries
Compute B^2 = [[9 + 3\beta, 15],[5\beta, 4 + 3\beta]] and impose B^2 - 5B - 6I = O
Diagonal gives 9 + 3\beta - 15 - 6 = 0 so \beta = 4 which also zeroes the remaining entry
Then B - A = [[2, 1],[3, 0 - 1]] and B + A = [[4, 5],[5, 5]] whose product is [[13, 15],[7, 10]]
Transpose of that product is [[13, 7],[15, 10]] which differs from [[13, 15],[7, 10]] so statement S1 is false
Also A + B = [[4, 5],[5, 5]] has determinant 20 - 25 = 0 - 5 and det adj equals det for 2 by 2 so statement S2 is true → (B)
1005:
Write A as 1 + 5m for m = 0 to 100 and B as 9 + 7k for k = 0 to 70
Equate terms via 1 + 5m = 9 + 7k so 5m - 7k = 8 with first solution m = 3 giving value 16
Successive common terms step by lcm 5 and 7 which is 35 so intersection is 16 + 35t
Bound 16 + 35t \leq 499 gives t = 0 to 13 so there are 14 common terms in all
Divisibility by 3 needs 16 + 35t \equiv 1 + 2t \equiv 0 mod 3 so t \equiv 1 mod 3
Values t = 1, 4, 7, 10, 13 give 5 such terms → (B)
1006:
Seven places with five digits each used at least once forces multiplicities 3, 1, 1, 1, 1 or 2, 2, 1, 1, 1
For pattern 3, 1, 1, 1, 1 choose the tripled digit in 5 ways
Arrange each such choice in 7! / 3! = 840 ways giving 5 \times 840 = 4200 numbers
For pattern 2, 2, 1, 1, 1 choose the two doubled digits in \binom{5}{2} = 10 ways
Arrange each such choice in 7! / (2! 2!) = 1260 ways giving 10 \times 1260 = 12600 numbers
Add the disjoint cases via 4200 + 12600 = 16800 → (C)
1007:
Use ratio \frac{\binom{36}{r + 1}}{\binom{35}{r}} = 36 / (r + 1) from factorial cancellation
Hence equation becomes 36 / (r + 1) = 6 / (k^2 - 3) so r + 1 = 6(k^2 - 3)
Valid r satisfies 0 \leq r \leq 35 so 1 \leq r + 1 \leq 36 with k^2 - 3 positive
Thus k^2 - 3 lies in 1 to 6 giving k^2 in 4 to 9 as the only possible values
Integer k forces k^2 = 4 or k^2 = 9 giving pairs (r, k) = (5, \pm 2) and (35, \pm 3)
Count distinct pairs as 2 + 2 = 4 in set S → (B)
1008:
Take class midpoints 7.5, 12.5, 17.5, 22.5, 27.5, 32.5 with frequencies 2, k, 28, 54, k + 1, 5
Total frequency N = 2 + k + 28 + 54 + k + 1 + 5 = 90 + 2k
Weighted sum equals 15 + 12.5k + 490 + 1215 + 27.5k + 27.5 + 162.5 = 1910 + 40k
Mean condition (1910 + 40k) / (90 + 2k) = 21 gives 1910 + 40k = 1890 + 42k so k = 10
Test x = 10 in options: 2x^2 - 23x - 10 = 0 - 40 while 4x^2 - 35x + 24 = 74 and 2x^2 - 35x + 98 = 0 - 52
Only 2x^2 - 19x - 10 = 200 - 190 - 10 = 0 holds so k is a root of that equation → (C)
1009:
Denote midpoints M_1 = (5 / 2, 7) and M_2 = (5 / 2, 3) and M_3 = (4, 5)
Recover vertices via A = M_2 + M_3 - M_1 = (4, 1) and B = M_1 + M_3 - M_2 = (4, 9)
Third vertex C = M_1 + M_2 - M_3 = (1, 5) completes the triangle from midpoints
Side lengths are AB = 8 with BC = 5 and CA = 5 from distance formula giving isosceles shape
Incentre equals (5A + 5B + 8C) / 18 = (48 / 18, 90 / 18) = (8 / 3, 5) so h = 8 / 3 and k = 5
Combine to get 3h + k = 8 + 5 = 13 → (C)
1010:
Since a < b major axis lies along y so e^2 = 1 - a^2 / b^2 = 5 / 9
Rearrange to get a^2 / b^2 = 4 / 9 so a^2 = 4b^2 / 9 linking the semiaxes
Point (4, 3) gives 16 / a^2 + 9 / b^2 = 1 as the ellipse condition
Substitute a^2 to get 36 / b^2 + 9 / b^2 = 45 / b^2 = 1 so b^2 = 45 and a^2 = 20
Latus rectum for vertical major axis equals 2a^2 / b = 40 / \sqrt{45}
Simplify 40 / \sqrt{45} = 40 / (3\sqrt{5}) = 8\sqrt{5} / 3 → (D)
1011:
Convert angles to degrees as \sin 10^\circ \sin 50^\circ \sin 70^\circ equals K
Use identity \sin 50^\circ \sin 70^\circ = \sin^2 60^\circ - \sin^2 10^\circ for the last two factors
Hence K = \sin 10^\circ (3 / 4 - \sin^2 10^\circ) = (3\sin 10^\circ - 4\sin^3 10^\circ) / 4
Triple angle gives 3\sin 10^\circ - 4\sin^3 10^\circ = \sin 30^\circ = 1 / 2 so K = 1 / 8
Then 10K\pi / 3 = 10\pi / 24 = 5\pi / 12 which is 75^\circ in degrees
Sine of 75^\circ equals (\sqrt{3} + 1) / (2\sqrt{2}) → (A)
1012:
Rewrite f(x) = \sin^2 x + \sin x \cos x = 1 / 2 + (\sin 2x - \cos 2x) / 2
Express \sin 2x - \cos 2x = \sqrt{2} \sin(2x - \pi / 4) so range is (1 - \sqrt{2}) / 2 to (1 + \sqrt{2}) / 2
Numerically range lies near 0 - 0.21 to 1 + 0.21 so only integers a = 0 and a = 1 can occur
For a = 0 need \sin x = 0 or \sin x + \cos x = 0 giving x = 0 - \pi, 0, \pi and x = 0 - \pi / 4, 3\pi / 4
That yields five distinct points in closed interval 0 - \pi to \pi for the zero case
For a = 1 write (\tan^2 x + \tan x) / (1 + \tan^2 x) = 1 so \tan x = 1 plus the \cos x = 0 cases
That yields x = \pi / 4, 0 - 3\pi / 4, \pi / 2, 0 - \pi / 2 giving four points so total 5 + 4 = 9 → (D)
1013:
Parametrize first line as x = 0 - 1 + 3\lambda with y = 0 - a + 5\lambda and z = 0 - b - 1 + 7\lambda
Parametrize second line as x = 2 + \mu with y = b + 4\mu and z = 2a + 7\mu
Intersection on xy plane forces z = 0 so 0 - b - 1 + 7\lambda = 0 and 2a + 7\mu = 0
Equal x gives 0 - 1 + 3\lambda = 2 + \mu so 3\lambda - \mu = 3 after rearrangement
Multiply by 7 and use 7\lambda = b + 1 with 7\mu = 0 - 2a to get 2a + 3b = 18
Equal y gives 0 - a + 5\lambda = b + 4\mu so 5(b + 1) + 8a = 7a + 7b giving a - 2b + 5 = 0
Solve a = 2b - 5 with 2a + 3b = 18 to get b = 4 and a = 3 so a + b = 7 → (C)
1014:
Put u = 3\vec{a} and v = 2\vec{b} so |u| = 6 and |v| = 6.
Write p = |u + v| and q = |u - v| so the expression is 3p + 4q.
By the parallelogram law p^2 + q^2 = 2|u|^2 + 2|v|^2 = 144.
By Cauchy-Schwarz (3p + 4q)^2 \leq (9 + 16)(p^2 + q^2) = 25 \times 144.
Hence 3p + 4q \leq 60 with equality for p : q = 3 : 4 which is attainable since |u \cdot v| stays within bounds.
Maximum value is 60 → (C)
1015:
Direction of L is perpendicular to both given vectors so d = (2, 2, 1) \times (1, 2, 2) = (2, -3, 2).
Hence L is (1, 1, 1) + t(2, -3, 2) for a scalar t.
Foot P from the origin satisfies OP \cdot d = 0 so 2(1 + 2t) - 3(1 - 3t) + 2(1 + 2t) = 0.
This simplifies to 1 + 17t = 0 so t = \frac{-1}{17}.
Thus P = (\frac{15}{17}, \frac{20}{17}, \frac{15}{17}) and a + b + c = \frac{50}{17}.
Therefore 34(a + b + c) = 100 → (C)
1016:
Put P(x) = x^3 - 5x^2 + ax + b and note \sqrt{x - 1} - 1 = \frac{x - 2}{\sqrt{x - 1} + 1}.
Since \log(x - 1) behaves like x - 2 near x = 2 the denominator behaves like \frac{(x - 2)^2}{2}.
A finite limit then forces P(2) = 0 and P'(2) = 0 where P'(x) = 3x^2 - 10x + a.
Now P'(2) = 12 - 20 + a = 0 gives a = 8 and P(2) = 4 + b = 0 gives b = -4.
Then P(x) = (x - 1)(x - 2)^2 so \frac{\sin P(x)}{P(x)} \rightarrow 1 and \frac{P(x)}{denominator} \rightarrow 2 giving m = 2.
Hence a + b + m = 8 - 4 + 2 = 6 → (B)
1017:
For x > 0 divide by y to get \frac{1}{y} \frac{dy}{dx} = 2 + \log x.
Integrate termwise using \int \log x dx = x \log x - x to obtain \log y = 2x + x \log x - x + C.
This simplifies to \log y = x + x \log x + C with one constant C.
Passing through (1, e) gives 1 = 1 + 0 + C so C = 0.
Hence \log y = x(1 + \log x) and at x = e this equals e(1 + 1) = 2e.
Therefore f(e) = e^{2e} → (C)
1018:
For x \neq 0 differentiate to get f'(x) = \frac{x \cos x - \sin x}{x^2}.
Zeros with x \neq 0 satisfy x \cos x - \sin x = 0 which is \tan x = x.
Also f(x) = 1 - \frac{x^2}{6} + \cdots near 0 so f'(0) = 0 and 0 is a critical point.
On each branch of \tan the function \tan x - x has derivative \tan^2 x \geq 0 so it is strictly increasing.
Checking signs at branch ends inside (-2\pi, 2\pi) leaves exactly one root each in (\frac{-3\pi}{2}, -\pi) and (\pi, \frac{3\pi}{2}) besides 0.
Hence there are 3 critical points in all → (B)
1019:
Split by the greatest integer using [x] = 0 on [0, 1) and [x] = 1 on [1, 2) and [x] = 2 on [2, 3).
Since 0! = 1 and 1! = 1 and 2! = 2 the divisors are 1 and 1 and 2 respectively.
An antiderivative of e^x + e^{-x} is e^x - e^{-x} on each subinterval.
The three parts give (e - \frac{1}{e}) + (e^2 - \frac{1}{e^2} - e + \frac{1}{e}) + \frac{1}{2}(e^3 - \frac{1}{e^3} - e^2 + \frac{1}{e^2}).
Cancelling e and \frac{1}{e} leaves \frac{1}{2}(e^2 + e^3 - \frac{1}{e^2} - \frac{1}{e^3}).
Collecting terms gives \frac{1}{2}(e^2 + e^3 - \frac{1}{e^2} - \frac{1}{e^3}) → (B)
1020:
Put u = y + 1 so \frac{du}{dx} = \frac{dy}{dx} and the equation becomes (1 + \sin x)\frac{du}{dx} + u \cos x = 0.
Separate to get \frac{1}{u} du = \frac{-\cos x}{1 + \sin x} dx.
Integrating gives \log|u| + \log|1 + \sin x| = C_1 so u(1 + \sin x) = C.
Condition y(0) = 0 gives u = 1 at x = 0 so 1 \times 1 = C and C = 1.
Hence y + 1 = \frac{1}{1 + \sin x} and y = \frac{-1}{2} gives \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{1 + \sin \alpha}.
Thus \sin \alpha = 1 so \alpha = \frac{\pi}{2} works → (D)
1021:
Need \log_{0.6}|\frac{2x - 5}{x^2 - 4}| \geq 0 with x \neq \pm 2 and x \neq \frac{5}{2}.
Since the base 0.6 is below 1 this means 0 < |\frac{2x - 5}{x^2 - 4}| \leq 1.
Squaring gives (x^2 - 4)^2 - (2x - 5)^2 \geq 0 which factors as (x - 1)^2(x^2 + 2x - 9) \geq 0.
With roots -1 - \sqrt{10} and -1 + \sqrt{10} this holds for x \leq -1 - \sqrt{10} or x \geq -1 + \sqrt{10} or x = 1.
Excluding x = \frac{5}{2} splits the right ray so a = -1 - \sqrt{10} and b = 1 and c = -1 + \sqrt{10} with d = e = \frac{5}{2}.
Sum gives a + b + c + d + e = -1 + 5 = 4 → (4)
1022:
Let S_n = \sum_{k = 1}^{n} a_k = 6n^3 so a_k = S_k - S_{k - 1} for k \geq 2.
Hence a_k = 6k^3 - 6(k - 1)^3 = 18k^2 - 18k + 6 for every k.
Differencing again gives a_{k + 1} - a_k = 36k so \frac{a_{k + 1} - a_k}{36} = k.
The required sum is therefore \sum_{k = 1}^{6} k^2.
Using \frac{n(n + 1)(2n + 1)}{6} at n = 6 gives \frac{6 \times 7 \times 13}{6} = 91.
Required value is 91 → (91)
1023:
With a > 0 positivity for all x needs discriminant below 0 so 8b^2 - 4ac < 0.
This simplifies to 2b^2 < ac with each of a and b and c in \lbrace 1, 2, 3, 4 \rbrace.
For b = 1 need ac > 2 which excludes only (1, 1) and (1, 2) and (2, 1) leaving 13 pairs.
For b = 2 need ac > 8 which holds only for (3, 3) and (3, 4) and (4, 3) and (4, 4) giving 4 pairs.
For b = 3 or b = 4 need ac > 18 or ac > 32 which is impossible so total favourable triples are 13 + 4 = 17 from 64.
Probability is \frac{17}{64} in lowest terms so m + n = 17 + 64 = 81 → (81)
1024:
Three axis points with equal intercepts force (0, 0) and (d, 0) and (0, d) with d > 0.
Centre is then (\frac{d}{2}, \frac{d}{2}) and radius satisfies r^2 = \frac{d^2}{2}.
Distance from the centre to x + y = 1 is \frac{|d - 1|}{\sqrt{2}}.
Chord length \sqrt{14} gives (\frac{\sqrt{14}}{2})^2 + \frac{(d - 1)^2}{2} = \frac{d^2}{2}.
Hence 14 + 2(d - 1)^2 = 2d^2 which reduces to 16 - 4d = 0 so d = 4.
Therefore r^2 = 8 → (8)
1025:
Put f(x) = \log_{2}(x^2 + 4) which is increasing on [0, 2\sqrt{3}].
Endpoint values are f(0) = 2 and f(2\sqrt{3}) = \log_{2} 16 = 4.
Inverse follows from y = \log_{2}(x^2 + 4) giving x = \sqrt{2^y - 4} = f^{-1}(y).
Second integral is exactly \int_{2}^{4} f^{-1}(y) dy over the image interval.
Area rule gives \int_{0}^{2\sqrt{3}} f + \int_{2}^{4} f^{-1} = 2\sqrt{3} \times 4 - 0 = 8\sqrt{3}.
Hence \alpha = 8\sqrt{3} and \alpha^2 = 64 \times 3 = 192 → (192)
1026:
\frac{1}{2} \epsilon_0 E^2 is the electric field energy density, so it has the dimensions of energy / volume
Energy is M L^2 T^{-2} and volume is L^3, so the ratio is M L^{-1} T^{-2}, giving a = 1, b = -1, c = -2
Then 2a - b + c = 2 + 1 - 2 = 1 → (B)
1027:
Young modulus is Y = F L / (A e) = 4 F L / (\pi d^2 e), with F = 100 N, L = 1.5 m, d = 8 \times 10^{-4} m, e = 5 \times 10^{-3} m, giving Y near 6.0 \times 10^{10} N / m^2
Fractional error adds as \Delta Y / Y = \Delta L / L + 2 \Delta d / d + \Delta e / e = 0.1 / 150 + 2 \times 0.001 / 0.08 + 0.001 / 0.5, about 0.0277
Absolute error is about 0.0277 \times 6.0 \times 10^{10} N / m^2, about 1.65 \times 10^9 N / m^2, so \alpha = 1.65 → (B)
1029:
Velocity is \vec{v} = 20t \hat{i} + 15t^2 \hat{j} m / s, so at t = 1 s momentum is \vec{p} = 0.1 \times (20 \hat{i} + 15 \hat{j}) = 2 \hat{i} + 1.5 \hat{j} kg m / s and A holds
Acceleration is \vec{a} = 20 \hat{i} + 30t \hat{j} m / s^2, so at t = 1 s force is \vec{F} = 2 \hat{i} + 3 \hat{j} N and B holds
With \vec{r} = 10 \hat{i} + 5 \hat{j} m at t = 1 s, angular momentum L_z = 10 \times 1.5 - 5 \times 2 = 5 J s, so the claimed 15 fails and C is false
Torque \tau_z = 10 \times 3 - 5 \times 2 = 20 N m, so D holds and the true set is A, B and D → (D)
1030:
Centripetal balance gives T = 2 \pi \sqrt{R^3 / (G M)}, so T is proportional to \sqrt{R^3 / M}
Hence T_2 / T_1 = \sqrt{(2R)^3 / (4M) \times (2M) / R^3} = \sqrt{4} = 2 → (B)
1031:
Angle is \theta = t^4 / 8 - t^3 / 3 rad, so \omega = t^3 / 2 - t^2 rad / s on differentiating once
Differentiating again gives \alpha = 3t^2 / 2 - 2t rad / s^2, and at t = 10 s this is 150 - 20 = 130 rad / s^2 → (C)
1032:
The dielectric of thickness d / 2 fills the full plate area, so the filled and empty halves are two capacitors in series
With C = \epsilon_0 A / d, the halves are K \epsilon_0 A / (d / 2) and \epsilon_0 A / (d / 2), giving 1 / C^{'} = (d / 2) / (K \epsilon_0 A) + (d / 2) / (\epsilon_0 A)
Thus C^{'} = 2K C / (K + 1) = 5C / 3 for K = 5, an increase of 2 / 3, about 66.67 percent → (B)
1033:
A diatomic gas has 5 quadratic degrees, so C_V = 5R / 2 and C_P = 7R / 2 with R in J / (mol K)
At constant pressure \Delta Q = C_P \Delta T, \Delta U = C_V \Delta T and \Delta W = R \Delta T for the same \Delta T
Hence \Delta Q : \Delta U : \Delta W = 7 / 2 : 5 / 2 : 1 = 7 : 5 : 2 → (D)
1034:
Joined by a wire the spheres reach the same potential V, and each capacitance is proportional to its radius
Field at a sphere surface is E = kQ / R^2 = V / R in V / m
So E_{S_1} / E_{S_2} = R_2 / R_1 = 18 / 8 = 9 / 4 → (D)
1036:
Point x lies on the axis of dipole A and on the equator of dipole B, from the viewed layout
Axial field is E_1 = 2k p_1 / x^3 along Ox and equatorial field is E_2 = k p_2 / x^3 across it, both in N / C
Resultant makes \theta with Ox where \tan \theta = E_2 / E_1 = p_2 / (2 p_1), and \theta = 60 degrees gives p_2 / p_1 = 2 \sqrt{3} → (B)
1037:
Clipping symmetrically at about +5 V and -5 V needs breakdown action in both polarities plus a series resistor to drop the remaining input
A single Zener clips asymmetrically and a diode network without series resistance cannot limit the current from a 20 V swing
A resistor in series with two oppositely connected Zeners breaks down near V_Z each way and gives the viewed flat tops → (D)
1038:
Induced emf scales as e_0 = N A B_0 \omega in V, so dissipated power P = e_{rms}^2 / R scales as N^2 A^2 / R
Wire resistance is R = \rho L / (\pi r^2) with copper length L = N \times 2 \pi R_c and coil area A = \pi R_c^2, so R scales as N \sqrt{A} / r^2
Thus P scales as N A^{3/2} r^2, and doubling N, doubling A and tripling r multiplies P by 2 \times 2 \sqrt{2} \times 9 = 36 \sqrt{2}
Writing 36 \sqrt{2} P = \sqrt{2} \alpha P gives \alpha = 36 → (A)
1039:
One long straight wire at distance r gives \mu_0 I / (4 \pi r) T and a half loop gives \mu_0 I / (4r) T in the same sense
Shape I has two active straights plus the half loop, so B_1 = \mu_0 I (2 + \pi) / (4 \pi r) T
Shape II has only the top straight active since the vertical wire is colinear with Q, so B_2 = \mu_0 I (1 + \pi) / (4 \pi r) T
Ratio B_1 / B_2 = (2 + \pi) / (1 + \pi) → (A)
1040:
At minimum deviation the ray is symmetric with r_1 = r_2 = A / 2 for apex angle A
Snell law \sin i = n \sin(A / 2) with n = 1.5 gives i near nA / 2 = 0.75 A rad for a thin prism
Deviation is \delta near (n - 1) A = 0.5 A rad, so i / \delta = 0.75 / 0.5 = 3 / 2 → (B)
1041:
Light goes from air \mu_1 = 1 to glass \mu_2 = 1.54 through one spherical surface of radius R = -20 cm with object distance u = -40 cm
Single surface formula \mu_2 / v - \mu_1 / u = (\mu_2 - \mu_1) / R gives 1.54 / v + 1 / 40 = -0.027 cm^{-1}, so v is about -29.6 cm, virtual
Magnification m = \mu_1 v / (\mu_2 u) is about 0.48, so a 2 cm object images about 0.96 cm tall, about 1 cm → (A)
1042:
Einstein relation is eV_s = hc / \lambda - hc / \lambda_0 with V_s in V and wavelengths in m
Thus 3eV_0 = hc / \lambda - \phi and eV_0 = hc / (2 \lambda) - \phi give 2eV_0 = hc / (2 \lambda) on subtracting
So eV_0 = hc / (4 \lambda) and \phi = hc / (4 \lambda), giving threshold \lambda_0 = 4 \lambda and \alpha = 4 → (B)
1043:
Electric amplitude is F_E = eE_0 N and magnetic amplitude is F_B = evB_0 N for charge e, speed v and fields in V / m and T
For a wave B_0 = E_0 / c, so F_E / F_B = c / v
With c = 3 \times 10^8 m / s and v = 1.5 \times 10^6 m / s the ratio is 200 → (A)
1044:
Bohr rule is L = nh / (2 \pi) J s, set equal to 3h / \pi J s
This gives n / 2 = 3, so n = 6
Energy E_6 = -13.6 / 36 eV, about -0.38 eV → (C)
1045:
Big radius is R = 10^{-3} m and volume conservation gives small radius r = R / 8 m for 512 drops
Area gain is \Delta A = 4 \pi (512 r^2 - R^2) = 28 \pi R^2, about 28 \pi \times 10^{-6} m^2
Energy T \Delta A with T = 0.08 N / m is about 7.04 \times 10^{-6} J, so \alpha = 7 → (B)
1046:
First minimum needs a \sin \theta = \lambda, so half width is \theta near \lambda / a rad
Full central width is 2 \lambda / a = 2 \times 628 \times 10^{-9} / (0.2 \times 10^{-3}) = 6.28 \times 10^{-3} rad
In degrees this is 6.28 \times 10^{-3} \times 180 / \pi, about 0.36 degrees, which is 36 \times 10^{-2} degrees → (36)
1047:
Here C_P = 3R and C_V = 2R J / (mol K), so \gamma = 3 / 2 = 1.5
With p_1 = 8 \times 10^5 Pa and V_1 = 0.15 m^3, adiabatic V_2 = V_1 (p_1 / p_2)^{1 / \gamma} = 0.15 \times 8^{2 / 3} = 0.6 m^3 for p_2 = 10^5 Pa
Work W = (p_1 V_1 - p_2 V_2) / (\gamma - 1) = (120000 - 60000) / 0.5 = 120000 J, which is 120 kJ → (120)
1048:
Force is \vec{F} = q \vec{v} \times \vec{B} with q = 10^{-6} C, \vec{v} = \hat{i} - 2 \hat{j} + 3 \hat{k} m / s and \vec{B} = 2 \hat{i} + 3 \hat{j} - 5 \hat{k} T
Cross product is \hat{i} + 11 \hat{j} + 7 \hat{k} T m / s, whose squared length is 1 + 121 + 49 = 171 m^2 T^2 / s^2
Magnitude is \sqrt{171} \times 10^{-6} N, so \alpha = 171 → (171)
1049:
Tension at a section balances the hanging load plus the wire length below it
Below l / 3 from the top there is 2l / 3 of wire weighing 2w / 3 N, so T = W + 2w / 3 N

1050:
